advice: Proposal: start from `existing-sme`, SHA-256 `3719c58530161598ab9a537a43be749a5287c8d8dbd35b855e5afea97cd15258`. Replace the full `n×n` transpose with a blocked transpose-and-pack in `gemm`: for each 32-row output panel, pack A directly into contiguous K-major panels, `packed_a[k][row]`, with panel width at most 32. Update the SME kernel to consume those panels and use the existing general tail handling. Allocate and free the packed buffer inside `gemm`; retain the fallback and all other benchmark settings. This removes a separate full-matrix transpose pass and may improve A locality during consumption. It is a falsifiable locality hypothesis, not a speed claim. Measure the complete timed `gemm` path, including allocation, packing, and consumption, for n=512 and all supported sizes.
risks: Packing adds writes and allocation, and panel access may cost more than the current transpose. The reported 32-wide panel is 64 KiB; A and B panels together equal the reported 128 KiB P-core L1D capacity, with no margin. Preserve FP32 MOPA order, selectors 0–3, general odd tails, n<=0 behavior, ABI, and tolerance. Check output and guard correctness across sizes, inspect candidate assembly for unexpected spills or redundant work, then compare repeated fresh AC measurements against unchanged paired controls. Do not infer a gain from instruction counts or attribute a joint result to this proposal alone.
